week.narrative: Developers shipped 5,842 new Spaces this week, all of them classifiable (100.0%). Conversational apps are the largest named use case at 903, ahead of image generation at 582 and data analysis at 461, though a residual "everything else" bucket of 1,822 sits above all of them. Vision-language is the most common technique at 7.0% of new Spaces, with agentic patterns at 6.5%; media and entertainment (9.7%) and consumer (9.4%) are the verticals most often pointed at. On the model side, 24,465 new models arrived, with Qwen the largest named family at 8,397.

cards.headline: Chat and assistants is the largest named thing people are building
cards.body: Of 5,842 new Spaces, 903 are chat and assistant interfaces — more than any other named use case. This is the default shape a developer reaches for when wrapping a language model into something someone else can touch.
cards.heroCaption: new Spaces built for chat and assistants

cards.headline: Generative media and document work form the second tier of use cases
cards.body: Image generation accounts for 582 new Spaces, voice and audio for 339, and document AI for 341. Together these sit behind conversational apps but describe a distinct kind of build: a single modality in, a usable artefact out.
cards.heroCaption: new Spaces built for image generation

cards.headline: Data analysis apps outnumber document AI and voice
cards.body: 461 new Spaces are built for data analysis, placing it third among named use cases. That puts spreadsheet-and-chart tooling ahead of both document AI at 341 and voice and audio at 339.
cards.heroCaption: new Spaces built for data analysis

cards.headline: Vision-language is the most common technique, with agentic patterns close behind
cards.body: 7.0% of new Spaces use vision-language, 6.5% use agentic patterns, and 5.3% are multimodal. Image-and-text understanding is now the technique developers reach for most often, and agent scaffolding is in the same band rather than trailing it.
cards.heroCaption: share of new Spaces using vision-language

cards.headline: Retrieval and tool use are thin next to the volume of chat and document apps
cards.body: RAG appears in 3.5% of new Spaces and tool use in 3.5% — the two lowest technique shares here. Yet 903 Spaces are chat and assistant interfaces and 341 are document AI, the exact places grounding and external calls tend to matter most.
cards.heroCaption: share of new Spaces using RAG

cards.headline: Enterprise productivity and retail trail the consumer-facing verticals
cards.body: Media and entertainment leads at 9.7% of new Spaces and consumer at 9.4%, while enterprise productivity sits at 5.7% and e-commerce and retail at 5.2%. Education (7.3%) and scientific research (7.1%) both come in ahead of the commercial verticals.
cards.heroCaption: share of new Spaces serving media and entertainment

cards.headline: Static pages ship more Spaces than Gradio does
cards.body: 3,088 new Spaces shipped as Static against 2,049 with Gradio, with Docker at 531 and Streamlit at 108. A large share of the week's output is therefore front-end or demo pages rather than a Python app framework wrapping a live model.
